issues.legal_issue: A civil court retains jurisdiction over a commercial loan-recovery suit when the claim does not arise under agricultural-tenancy law and the security is merely collateral to the debt.
material_facts: A bank advanced a demand loan to an agriculturist in the ordinary course of its commercial business, and the borrower executed a promissory note.
The borrower hypothecated standing crops and mortgaged agricultural land as security for repayment; two other defendants guaranteed repayment.
After the loan was not repaid, the bank sued to recover the debt on the promissory note and guarantees, with sale of the mortgaged property sought only if the decree was not paid.
The suit was primarily for recovery of the loan and was not a suit to enforce a mortgage created under the agricultural-tenancy legislation.
No applicable listed suit or other remedy under that legislation covered the bank’s commercial debt-recovery claim.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had jurisdiction to entertain the bank’s suit. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the trial court’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 207 and 256 of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955, civil-court jurisdiction is barred for suits specified in the Third Schedule, suits based on a cause of action for which relief could be obtained in such a suit, and matters arising under the Act for which it provides a remedy. Entry 35 of the Third Schedule applies only to a matter arising under the Act. Section 43 concerns specified mortgages or hypothecations of tenancy interests for obtaining specified loans; a commercial bank loan does not become a matter arising under the Act merely because agricultural land is offered as collateral. Jurisdiction depends on the substance, not the form, of the suit. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_recovery_suit and commercial_lending_transaction and primary_claim_is_debt_repayment and security_is_collateral and claim_outside_special_tenancy_remedies

predicates.civil_recovery_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking recovery of a debt.
predicates.commercial_lending_transaction: A lender advanced money in the ordinary course of its commercial lending business.
predicates.primary_claim_is_debt_repayment: The claim was primarily based on the borrower’s promise to repay and any guarantees, rather than on enforcement of security.
predicates.security_is_collateral: The borrower provided property or other security only as collateral for repayment of the debt.
predicates.claim_outside_special_tenancy_remedies: The debt-recovery claim did not concern a matter arising under the special agricultural-tenancy regime and was not one for which that regime provided a remedy.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a civil debt-recovery suit arising from commercial lending, relies primarily on the debt and guarantees, and uses security only as collateral for a claim outside special tenancy remedies, the civil court has jurisdiction.
